# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platforms: iOS/macOS. Every hero image is rasterized together with its headline, panoramas are cropped through landmarks, low-resolution assets are stretched and all image descriptions say Image. Missing images collapse article context.

# Apple HIG: Platform and task adaptation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the person’s primary task and the target platform before translating a screen. Read that platform’s procedure; use Principles to resolve hierarchy and Designing for games only for gameplay.
2. Compare navigation, window/scene model, primary input, attention duration and state restoration. Preserve the product task while changing the interaction appropriate to the destination platform.
3. For device changes such as opening an iPhone Duo or resizing an iPad window, specify what selection, editing state and route survive each transition.
4. Deliver a platform-decision matrix or an adaptation patch, with concrete acceptance scenarios for each materially different interaction.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify what people need to understand or do with the content: compare data, read text, inspect imagery or interact with embedded web content. Enter that topic procedure.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

# Apple HIG: Integrate a capability into the product task

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the product benefit and capability prerequisites before entering the technology-specific procedure. Avoid adding a system integration solely to decorate an existing flow.
2. Define consent/account/capability availability and the meaningful result, cancel, failure and recovery paths applicable to that integration. Keep sensitive information and system ownership clear.
3. Preserve supplied branding, hardware and platform qualifications. HIG states experience expectations; verify current APIs against implementation documentation when writing framework-specific code.
4. Deliver an integration contract or correction in the existing stack, with source-supported choices, fallbacks and evidence limits. Do not claim a payment, health, spatial or connected-device runtime test from a static specimen.

# Make the iPhone task usable in the hand

Read [Designing for iOS](../../references/designing-for-ios.md). Inspect the current task, its entry and return points, supported orientations, input, and any supplied implementation. Distinguish a brief check from extended work. For a review, anchor problems to supplied screens/behavior; for design or adaptation, revise the requested artifact in its existing stack.

Choose what must remain immediately visible during the task. A brief check needs its result and primary action close together; extended editing can expose additional controls without crowding the initial screen. Put frequent touch actions within comfortable reach, generally toward the middle/lower display, while preserving system navigation and swipe-back behavior. Move secondary commands into a short discoverable path rather than shrinking every control to fit.

Trace interruption and resumption: preserve the selected item, draft, or playback context when another app takes focus. Specify portrait/landscape and enlarged-text rearrangements without inventing a new navigation hierarchy for each orientation. Use touch and onscreen keyboard as the baseline, then offer appropriate voice or accessory paths. Add location, biometric, payment, or motion features only when their benefit reduces task effort and access is appropriate.

For repeated out-of-app actions, choose a relevant system entrypoint and a precise destination: a quick action starts an action, search opens the found content, and a widget exposes a useful glance. Do not add every entrypoint to every app.

**Before → decision → after:** A parcel app opens a dense desktop-style table and requires opening three menus to find the latest delivery. A handheld glance needs delivery state first. The revised home screen shows the active parcel and “Show pickup code,” keeps history one step away, and returns a widget tap to that parcel rather than a generic home screen.

Deliver a revised screen/flow or implementation plus interruption, orientation, and text-size acceptance checks. Fail if the primary action becomes unreachable, Back conflicts with a custom gesture, or resuming loses work. Screenshot review cannot establish touch comfort or actual system integration; state pending device checks.

For detailed adaptation use [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md); for custom touch gestures use [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md); for a chosen glance use [Widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md).

# Give desktop work desktop control

Read [Designing for macOS](../../references/designing-for-macos.md). Inspect the current task, document/content model, windows, commands, and interruption behavior. Determine whether the request is a design, review, or port. Preserve the existing stack and distinguish observed behavior from proposals or missing runtime evidence.

Choose window boundaries around useful units of work. If documents or parallel comparisons benefit from independent windows, retain their own selections and edits. If one workspace suffices, make it resizable and avoid unnecessary modal navigation. Plan full screen for focused work without making it the only usable arrangement. Keep essential commands reachable even when a window is partly offscreen.

Build a command inventory from the task. Put app commands in the menu bar, give common operations appropriate shortcuts, and ensure a keyboard-only completion path. Align toolbar/contextual controls with those same actions and availability states. Use pointer precision for selection and editing rather than inflating a phone-style interface across the display. Preserve conventional file opening/saving and relevant Dock-menu behavior.

Specify app activation changes: switching away and back must preserve work and clearly distinguish the active target for commands. Offer customization where different work styles justify it, such as tools or window arrangement; do not require customization before basic use.

**Before → decision → after:** A photo catalog port displays every album as a full-screen drill-down and exposes Export only through a floating touch menu. Desktop comparison needs persistent context and a discoverable command. After, an album sidebar and resizable detail area support selection; File > Export and a keyboard command act on that selection, and optional second windows compare collections without losing the original state.

Deliver the revised window/command model or implementation, with a keyboard path and activation scenario. Fail if menu and toolbar act on different selections, switching apps loses edits, or resizing hides the only completion action. Linux inspection does not establish actual menu-bar integration, multi-display behavior, or native keyboard accessibility.

Use [Keyboards](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-keyboards/SKILL.md) for command details, [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for window constraints, and [Mac Catalyst](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-mac-catalyst/SKILL.md) when adapting an iPad app through that technology.

# Separate image presentation from action

Read [the image-view guide](../../references/image-views.md). Use the following as application advice, preserving the requested stack.

Inspect the image assets and container, target platform, intended focal content, and whether the request is to create, review, or adapt. Determine whether the image is decorative, informative, editable, or an action. Record intrinsic resolution/aspect ratio, crop/fit behavior, overlays, and animation source when available; a screenshot cannot establish frame preparation or input semantics.

Choose fitting from the content's purpose: preserve the whole image when cropping loses information; allow deliberate cropping when the focal subject survives. Do not stretch photographs to satisfy a container. If activation performs an action, use button semantics rather than attaching an unexplained gesture to a display image. On Mac, choose an image well for copy/paste/drag/Delete editing. Prefer symbols or template imagery for interface glyphs rather than embedding their appearance as arbitrary pictures.

Apply the choice in code or supply an annotated container/asset specification; reviews must identify a crop, semantic, or legibility defect with a concrete repair. For text overlays, inspect both bright and dark image regions and provide supporting treatment where needed. Prepare animation frames consistently rather than depending on repeated runtime rescaling. For tvOS retain intended layered transparency; for visionOS choose a window image, spatial presentation, or scene mechanism deliberately instead of flattening every image. The guide mentions implementation capabilities, not proof that a supplied framework supports them.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a museum map stretches into a portrait card, with a “View route” gesture on the picture. Decision: distortion damages map meaning and the action lacks button behavior. After: fit the complete map within the card and provide a named `View Route` image/button action; decorative framing remains outside its accessible name.

Deliver the changed asset/container behavior and semantic purpose. Verify key content survives aspect changes, overlays remain readable, and actionable imagery works through keyboard/assistive activation. Fail for hidden essential content, stretched meaning, or an actionable image with no name/role. Report native spatial/layered rendering as unverified without its runtime.

Load [image-wells](../../../apple-hig-selection-and-input/.topics/apple-hig-image-wells/SKILL.md) for editing, [buttons](../../../apple-hig-menus-and-actions/.topics/apple-hig-buttons/SKILL.md) for action, or [images](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-images/SKILL.md) for asset strategy.

# Match the image asset to its presentation

Read [Images](../../references/images.md). Inspect source dimensions, logical displayed size, supported densities/platforms, profiles, format, and whether the task is asset design, review, or adaptation. Preserve the chosen production pipeline where it can satisfy the requirements. Do not infer pixel quality from a filename or a scaled design preview.

Choose a format by content: scalable flat art/glyphs, photos, raster artwork, and stereo photos have different needs. Use the guide's platform density requirements and preserve embedded profiles. Calculate actual required pixels from logical points and density for 2D displays; visionOS points are angular, so distance and close inspection affect raster sufficiency. Balance higher resolution/filtering with file and runtime costs rather than maximizing every image.

For tvOS focus artwork, separate foreground information from supporting layers and provide an opaque background, crop-safe margins, and restrained depth. Distinguish bundled assets from downloadable runtime layers; `.lcr` is not the bundle format. For watchOS, flatten against a known solid background when possible, while retaining alpha for template imagery that must tint.

For visionOS stereo photos, preserve spatial metadata and choose presentation that permits comfortable depth adjustment. A generated spatial scene is a separate deliberate interaction; avoid generating many simultaneously or surrounding it with competing depth. Place photos/scenes in their own window/sheet where possible and keep immersive viewing UI restrained.

**Before → decision → after:** A TV gallery downloads a single transparent poster layer whose title clips when focused. Decision: focus movement needs a stable backing and safe foreground content. After, layered artwork uses an opaque background, separated title/subject, and enough crop margin verified through focus previews.

Deliver an asset/export manifest plus corrected assets or specific review. Fail if required-density output blurs at its intended size, profiles are absent, focus crops essential content, or stereo metadata is lost. Report file-level checks separately from actual TV/device/spatial comfort testing; Linux cannot establish the latter.

For launcher stacks use [App icons](../apple-hig-app-icons/SKILL.md); for color-space decisions use [Color](../apple-hig-color/SKILL.md); for spatial presentation use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md).

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Preserve readable hierarchy as text grows

Read [Typography](../../references/typography.md). Inspect the actual text roles, font files/styles, platform, viewing context, and resizing behavior. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Use the guide's platform style/size tables when exact values matter; do not reproduce the entire specification or confuse its minimum with a comfortable default.

Assign semantic roles before choosing sizes: title, body, supporting detail, and actionable label need a clear relationship. Prefer system text styles and runtime font APIs so optical design/tracking adapt to size. If a custom face is needed, verify weight/legibility and provide equivalent text-size and Bold Text behavior; thin faces may need more size than the table suggests. Use loose leading for sustained/wide reading, avoiding tight leading across three or more lines.

Decide how content expands. Grow containers, permit labels to wrap, stack timestamps/glyphs, and reduce columns rather than aggressively truncating essential reading. Scale meaningful glyphs with the text. Preserve hierarchy while prioritizing the content people intend to read; not every decorative/transient number must grow identically.

Apply platform differences: macOS has no Dynamic Type, so use appropriate standard-control fonts and explicit product text accommodations rather than promising that API behavior. On visionOS, favor readable 2D text, explicit styles for New York, little extrusion, and viewer-facing object labels; do not rely on cast shadows against unpredictable surroundings. Watch uses its own font conventions, including complication typography.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a book list fixes custom thin titles to one line and leaves status glyphs tiny at larger text sizes. Decision: reading and status must remain usable together. After, titles use a legible role/weight, wrap into growing rows, supporting text stacks, and meaningful glyphs scale while selection/actions stay available.

Deliver corrected type roles, resizing rules, or implementation with supported-size examples. Fail if essential content is clipped without a full-text route, hierarchy collapses, or Bold Text/custom sizing breaks controls. Record tested sizes and actual font measurements; device-distance legibility, native shaping, and spatial comfort need supported execution.

Use [Layout](../apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for reflow, [Accessibility](../apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for task-level access, or [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for mixed-script alignment.

# Expose the task's structure without relying on sight

Read [VoiceOver](../../references/voiceover.md). Inspect the task, actual accessibility semantics when available, visible content, dynamic updates, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the existing stack. A screenshot cannot establish spoken names, rotor behavior, focus order, or successful nonvisual operation; distinguish proposals from inspected runtime semantics.

Name important controls by actual function, improve unhelpful generic labels, and synchronize descriptions/values with changing content. Describe meaningful imagery only for information the image conveys beyond nearby captions; hide decoration from navigation. For charts, expose a concise purpose plus accessible equivalents for every interaction, not merely a label saying “Chart.”

Build navigation structure from the task. Give pages short unique titles and meaningful section headings. Express grouping, links, ordering, and relationships otherwise conveyed by proximity/alignment, following locale reading order and grouping captions with their own images. Mark headings/links for rotor navigation and notify assistive technologies of relevant content/layout changes without inventing untested announcement behavior.

On visionOS, custom-gesture apps do not normally receive hand input while VoiceOver exploration is active. Direct Gesture mode changes that relationship and disables standard VoiceOver gestures; provide an alternative task route instead of requiring every person to switch modes or depend on custom hands.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a sales chart exposes one unlabeled canvas and decorative stars interrupt the reading sequence, while changing a date updates only the visual title. Decision: nonvisual readers need structure, current values, and equivalent chart actions. After, a named section describes the chart's purpose, date controls expose current values, accessible summaries/actions cover comparisons, decorations leave navigation, and relevant updates are represented through supported semantics.

Deliver a semantic name/role/value/group/order specification or implementation with a nonvisual task walkthrough. Fail if a necessary action is unnamed/unreachable, values become stale, captions detach, or chart interaction has no equivalent. Report actual VoiceOver/rotor/device tests separately; Linux/static checks cannot claim screen-reader execution.

On 2D displays the pixel-to-point mapping depends on density; in visionOS points are angular and scale with viewing distance. ## Resolution Provide bitmap assets for every supported density: @1x means one pixel per point, @2x two, @3x three. Supply @2x for iPadOS/watchOS, @2x and @3x for iOS, @1x and @2x for macOS/tvOS, and at least @2x for visionOS according to viewing needs. Mark scale in filenames and asset catalogs. Inspect assets on actual supported devices to catch stretching, pixelation, and compression that design previews can miss. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS/iPadOS/macOS rules are listed. ### tvOS Use layers, transparency, scaling, and motion to reinforce focus and depth. #### Parallax effect The system raises, lights, and gently moves a focused item; after inactivity the focused item expands and other content dims. Layered artwork is required for this treatment. #### Layered images Use 2–5 layers. Layering is mandatory for the app icon and encouraged for other focusable artwork, including Top Shelf. Standard views and focus APIs apply the effect automatically. Place key objects and text in front, supporting content/shadows in the middle, and an opaque background behind. A transparent background causes an error. Keep depth subtle, leave a crop-safe margin especially on foreground layers, and preview through design tools plus an actual TV. Artwork can be bundled or downloaded. For server-delivered layers, generate `.lcr` runtime images from LSR/Photoshop with Xcode’s `layerutil`; these download-oriented files should not be embedded in the app. Apple’s Parallax Previewer/Exporter can help check clipping and scaling. ### visionOS Prefer vectors for 2D art because size and angle vary broadly and image pixels need not align to display pixels. App icons use 2–3 layers. A @2x raster can work at ordinary distance but may blur close up; higher resolutions increase file size and runtime cost, especially beyond @6x. Apply high-quality filtering when exceeding @2x, balancing clarity and performance. #### Spatial photos and spatial scenes A spatial photo is stereo imagery plus spatial metadata, captured on devices such as iPhone 15 Pro or newer, Vision Pro, or another compatible camera. A spatial scene derives a head-responsive 3D/parallax presentation from 2D imagery. RealityKit supports both. Use stereo HEIC with spatial metadata so visionOS recognizes photos and supplies comfort treatments. Prefer feathered glass behind overlaid text to add contrast and soften stereo detail. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. ## Contents - [Ensuring legibility](#Ensuring-legibility) - [Conveying hierarchy](#Conveying-hierarchy) - [Using system fonts](#Using-system-fonts) - [Using custom fonts](#Using-custom-fonts) - [Supporting Dynamic Type](#Supporting-Dynamic-Type) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) - [Resources](#Resources) - [Change log](#Change-log) ## Ensuring legibility Test type at real viewing distances, lighting conditions, and supported devices. Enlarge hard-to-read text, improve foreground/background contrast, or choose a more legible face. Prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold over Ultralight/Thin/Light, especially at small sizes. Thin custom faces often need sizes above the recommendations. |Platform|Default|Minimum| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| ## Conveying hierarchy Combine size, weight, and color to distinguish levels, and preserve those relationships as text grows. Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. New York is a complementary serif family. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. SF offers widths such as Condensed/Expanded and weights from Ultralight through Black; equivalent SF Symbol weights enable precise matching. Use semantic text styles to express hierarchy through coordinated weight, size, and leading, and to inherit Dynamic Type/accessibility adjustments where supported. Modify symbolic traits for emphasis or line spacing when justified. Loose leading supports long passages or wide columns; tight leading can fit constrained rows, but avoid it for three or more lines. Access system fonts through platform APIs (`default`, `serif`, and the font-design constants), without embedding the files. Runtime tracking adapts by size automatically; mockups may need the tracking values below. ## Using custom fonts Check custom faces against platform size recommendations and actual conditions. Implement Dynamic Type and Bold Text behavior equivalent to the system faces. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can support Dynamic Type in games; if unsuitable, offer a separate text-size adjustment. ## Supporting Dynamic Type Dynamic Type is available in iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. Test every supported size, including Larger Accessibility Text on iPhone/iPad. Scale meaningful glyphs as well as text; SF Symbols integrate automatically. Preserve useful information at the largest accessibility size rather than aggressively truncating. Give labels enough lines and avoid truncation in scrolling regions unless a detail view exposes the full text. Stack inline timestamps/glyphs beneath or above primary text, grow containers, and reduce columns when width becomes cramped. Keep important content toward the top and the overall hierarchy stable. ## Platform considerations ### iOS, iPadOS SF Pro is standard; New York is also available. ### macOS SF Pro is standard and New York is available to Mac Catalyst apps. macOS has no Dynamic Type. # Preserve relationships while available space changes

Read [Layout](../../references/layout.md). Inspect content priority, navigation, controls, supported environments, constraints, and current implementation. Identify design/review/adaptation mode and keep the existing layout system. Record actual available space and text/localization conditions; device names alone are insufficient evidence for a breakpoint.

Start with relationships: align peers, group related items, indent subordinates, and reveal secondary choices progressively. Place important content toward the leading/top region in the locale's reading order. Separate backgrounds that can extend beneath bars from important content/actions that must respect safe regions.

Choose adaptations from available width/height and environmental values, not a phone/tablet or portrait/landscape guess. Preserve selection, content, functionality, and idiom when columns collapse, actions overflow, or horizontal rows stack for larger text. Test the smallest and largest useful layouts first, then intermediate resizing, longer localization, direction changes, and display accommodations. Crop decorative backgrounds without distorting aspect ratio or hiding essential imagery.

Apply platform conditions deliberately: Mac essential controls cannot depend on a bottom edge that may be offscreen; TV content needs the guide's overscan insets and focus-expansion room; Watch normally needs very few side-by-side actions. visionOS windows/volumes should resize, use meaningful bounds, and avoid inline 3D crowding controls; use separate volumes for model-centric work. Read numeric platform specifications from the guide rather than generalizing one platform's spacing.

**Before → decision → after:** A reading list positions Delete at a fixed bottom coordinate and fixes each row to one line. Decision: resized windows and enlarged titles need flow-based layout. After, row height/wrapping adapt, secondary actions remain reachable through contextual overflow, and the selected article persists when the sidebar collapses.

Deliver corrected layouts/constraints or implementation plus an environment matrix. Fail if a required action disappears, related items detach, content overlaps hardware/bars, or resizing changes the task's meaning. Report tested dimensions/settings; static or Linux checks cannot establish native safe-area/focus behavior absent supported execution.

Use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md) for text behavior, [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for direction, and [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md) for 3D position/scale.

# Typography Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. ## Contents - [Ensuring legibility](#Ensuring-legibility) - [Conveying hierarchy](#Conveying-hierarchy) - [Using system fonts](#Using-system-fonts) - [Using custom fonts](#Using-custom-fonts) - [Supporting Dynamic Type](#Supporting-Dynamic-Type) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) - [Resources](#Resources) - [Change log](#Change-log) ## Ensuring legibility Test type at real viewing distances, lighting conditions, and supported devices. Enlarge hard-to-read text, improve foreground/background contrast, or choose a more legible face. Prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold over Ultralight/Thin/Light, especially at small sizes. Thin custom faces often need sizes above the recommendations. |Platform|Default|Minimum| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| ## Conveying hierarchy Combine size, weight, and color to distinguish levels, and preserve those relationships as text grows. Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. New York is a complementary serif family. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. SF offers widths such as Condensed/Expanded and weights from Ultralight through Black; equivalent SF Symbol weights enable precise matching. Use semantic text styles to express hierarchy through coordinated weight, size, and leading, and to inherit Dynamic Type/accessibility adjustments where supported. Modify symbolic traits for emphasis or line spacing when justified. Loose leading supports long passages or wide columns; tight leading can fit constrained rows, but avoid it for three or more lines. Access system fonts through platform APIs (`default`, `serif`, and the font-design constants), without embedding the files. Runtime tracking adapts by size automatically; mockups may need the tracking values below. ## Using custom fonts Check custom faces against platform size recommendations and actual conditions. Implement Dynamic Type and Bold Text behavior equivalent to the system faces. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can support Dynamic Type in games; if unsuitable, offer a separate text-size adjustment. ## Supporting Dynamic Type Dynamic Type is available in iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. Test every supported size, including Larger Accessibility Text on iPhone/iPad. Scale meaningful glyphs as well as text; SF Symbols integrate automatically. Preserve useful information at the largest accessibility size rather than aggressively truncating. Give labels enough lines and avoid truncation in scrolling regions unless a detail view exposes the full text. Stack inline timestamps/glyphs beneath or above primary text, grow containers, and reduce columns when width becomes cramped. Keep important content toward the top and the overall hierarchy stable. ## Platform considerations ### iOS, iPadOS SF Pro is standard; New York is also available. ### macOS SF Pro is standard and New York is available to Mac Catalyst apps. macOS has no Dynamic Type. Match standard-control typography with the relevant NSFont methods: `controlContentFont`, `labelFont`, `menuFont`, `menuBarFont`, `messageFont`, `paletteFont`, `titleBarFont`, `toolTipsFont`, `userFont`, `userFixedPitchFont`, `boldSystemFont`, and `systemFont`, each with its `ofSize:` parameter. ### tvOS SF Pro is standard, with New York also available. ### visionOS SF Pro is standard; specify text styles explicitly when using New York. Body/title Dynamic Type styles are bolder, and Extra Large Title 1/2 support wide editorial compositions. Prefer readable 2D text with little or no extrusion. Test full-scale designs through different viewing scales. Default white text contrasts with glass; test custom colors against diverse surroundings. Without a container background, bold can improve visibility; do not rely on unpredictable cast shadows. Billboard labels associated with 3D objects toward the viewer, normally rotating around the y-axis so the baseline stays perpendicular to the line of sight. ### watchOS SF Compact is standard, New York is available, and complications use SF Compact Rounded. ## Specifications Values below preserve the source’s factual measurements. Sizes, leading, and line heights are in points; tracking is given in thousandths of an em and points. Emphasis can be applied through SwiftUI `bold()` or UIKit `UIFontDescriptor` `traitBold`; the resulting emphasized weight varies by style. Use semantic APIs in production instead of freezing all layout to these reference values. ### iOS, iPadOS Dynamic Type sizes #### xSmall |Style|Weight|Size, pt|Leading, pt|Emphasis| |---|---|---|---|---| |Large Title|Regular|31|38|Bold| |Title 1|Regular|25|31|Bold|

# Layout Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Use predictable relationships among content and controls while adapting to the actual available space. ## Visual hierarchy Prioritize important content toward the top and leading edge in reading order. Use system components for RTL adaptation. Align related items, indent subordinate items, and group relationships with space, containers, or separators. Reveal secondary choices progressively through disclosure, menus, nested views, or scrollable media sections. Distinguish navigation/controls with Liquid Glass and scroll-edge treatments; extend full-window backgrounds under bars and sidebars. A background extension effect can mirror and blur imagery under adjacent components instead of hiding essential original art. ## Adaptability Handle size classes, display sizes, orientation/aspect ratio, Dynamic Island, external displays, Display Zoom, resizable windows, text changes, localized length/direction/fonts, and date/number formats. Use SwiftUI or Auto Layout, safe areas, margins, and layout modifiers. Orientation-locked games must still resize. With large text, stack horizontal content, increase row height, and allow wrapping. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can supply Dynamic Type in games. Preview smallest/largest layouts first, then multiple devices, localizations, sizes, iPad resizing, and iPhone Mirroring. Scale backgrounds to fill without distorting aspect ratio; extreme wide/short or narrow/tall windows may crop much more than standard displays. ### Size classes Each axis is compact or regular, describing available width or height rather than device type or orientation. All four combinations can occur as apps resize, multitask, or mirror. Base layout on these environmental values, not idiom/orientation guesses. Preserve functionality across classes while changing how much is exposed, such as sidebar versus tabs or visible actions versus overflow. The platform idiom remains the same during resizing, so preserve its familiar character. ## Guides and safe areas Layout guides supply rectangular regions for alignment, spacing, margins, and readable text widths; custom guides can add app-specific structure. Safe areas exclude edge obstructions such as camera hardware, status bars, tab bars, and toolbars. Keep important content and controls within the appropriate safe regions. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS rules are listed. ### macOS Do not rely on the bottom of a window for essential controls because it may sit below the physical display. Avoid placing content behind the top camera housing. ### tvOS Inset primary content 60 pt vertically and 80 pt horizontally to withstand TV overscan/settings. Leave enough focus padding for system enlargement so focused items do not obscure important information. #### Grids Use consistent row/column spacing, sufficient room for enlargement, and symmetrical partial items at both horizontal edges. Add extra separation above and below row titles. UIKit collection flow layout derives the column count from item width and spacing. Source grid measurements follow; all use 40 pt horizontal gaps and a minimum 100 pt vertical gap between unfocused rows. #### Two-column grid Unfocused item width: 860 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Three-column grid Unfocused item width: 560 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Four-column grid Unfocused item width: 410 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Five-column grid Unfocused item width: 320 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Six-column grid Unfocused item width: 260 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Seven-column grid Unfocused item width: 217 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Eight-column grid Unfocused item width: 184 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Nine-column grid Unfocused item width: 160 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. ### visionOS Support resizing in windows and volumes; center content horizontally at very large sizes. Set minimum/maximum bounds only to avoid overlaps or unwieldy layouts, not to disable resizing. Use inline 3D content sparingly for meaningful additions; inset it so it avoids controls and window edges. Prefer volumes or immersive spaces for large/model-centric content. Open supplemental content in an adjacent window, reserving ornaments for interactive app controls. Space controls so hover feedback remains distinct; regular buttons should have centers at least 60 pt apart. ### watchOS Normally use no more than three glyph buttons or two text buttons side by side. Full-width text controls usually work best; two short labels can fit on a non-scrolling screen. Support autorotation when people may show content, such as a photo or QR code, to another person or reader instead of always sleeping on wrist-away movement. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 9, 2026, September 9, 2025, June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, September 9, 2024, June 10, 2024, February 2, 2024, December 5, 2023, September 15, 2023, June 21, 2023, September 14, 2022.
